commitResults.messageTitle: Store and list tasks in memory
Represent tasks and track completion status
Support todo, deadline, and event tasks
Handle invalid commands with clear exceptions
Represent supported commands with an enum

commitResults.messageBody: Tasks are lost whenever Nori exits, which makes the task list unsuitable for continued use.\n\nAdd a small text-file storage layer and persist the list after successful commands. Load saved tasks at startup so task types and completion states survive restarts.

Deadline dates are stored as unvalidated text, so invalid dates are accepted and valid dates are not presented consistently.\n\nRepresent deadline dates with LocalDate. Accept ISO dates for reliable parsing and format them for readable task output while retaining ISO text in storage.

Nori coordinates parsing, storage, task management, and console interaction in one class. This makes each responsibility harder to understand and change independently.\n\nExtract focused Parser, TaskList, Storage, and Ui components. Keep Nori as the small coordinator while preserving the existing command behavior.

All classes are in the default package, which obscures the boundary between application services and task models.\n\nPlace the application components in the nori package and the task hierarchy in nori.task. Keep the package structure compact to match the current project size.

The supplied Gradle configuration targets the starter Duke class and artifact name.\n\nPoint the application plugin at nori.Nori and name the executable artifact nori.jar so the existing wrapper can build and run this project.

Parsing and persistence sit at the boundaries between user input, disk data, and the task model. Regressions in either area can make commands fail or saved tasks unusable.\n\nAdd focused JUnit tests for command parsing, missing storage files, and a task save-load round trip.

The main components have class comments but most public constructors and methods do not explain their contracts.\n\nAdd concise Javadoc for public APIs, command values, and shared task behavior. Keep comments focused on purpose, parameters, results, and failure conditions.

Several constructs do not follow the required basic and intermediate layout and access rules.\n\nIndent switch cases consistently, format the array initializer, prevent Parser instantiation, and restrict the abstract Task constructor to subclasses.

Users cannot locate a task without scanning the entire list. This becomes inconvenient as the list grows.\n\nAdd a case-insensitive find command that matches description substrings and reports empty searches or no results clearly.

Package organization moved the main class, and Week 3 used widespread Codex assistance.\n\nCorrect the IntelliJ source path and disclose the scope of AI assistance so setup instructions and reuse attribution remain accurate.
